sources.reason: Historical assembly modules with annotated dungeon generator, parser, renderer and scanned listing. Repository describes original 1982 source; missing-macros file indicates reconstruction support. Provenance/build completeness not independently certified.

Despite index-style repository description, self-contained HTML implements disk overlay reading/writing and Shift-JIS handling plus archive/image/script tools. No data uploaded or candidate code executed in this review; format completeness untested.

Driver-behaviour reconstruction uses Python control logic and fmgen sound core, not CPU emulation of the whole OS. Built-in instrument bank but external rhythm WAVs needed; optional LFO and high-fidelity claims remain upstream-only.

Sequence splitting/combining, instrument conversion and MIDI export source for GEMS sound data. Root toolkit is distinct from original sound driver and signature-only datasets; no equivalence tests run.
Source-available 68000 sequence driver with Z80 PCM playback and SGDK integration. Windows toolchain/Wine requirements explicit; experimental System C2 branch is not promoted as mainline support.

Annotated banking, interrupt interception, cheat-state and firmware source. Distinct cartridge firmware, not a game port; upstream notes timing side effects and unused BIOS/debug material.

Named decompressor and broader disassembly alongside incomplete track editor. In-memory editing and compression exist; ROM reinsertion, layout auto-patching and several metadata editors remain unfinished. Keep coherent root project.

ROM-driven Forth primitive discovery, patch tooling and live-analysis probes. Forth-threaded data is not ordinary linear 6502 code; source toolkit is substantive despite omitted generated game listing. Hardware and patch claims remain upstream-tested only.

decisions.title: Disc Image Studio CPC disk tools
decisions.reason: DSK/AMSDOS/CP-M image tooling with actual header parser and multiple utilities. README retains old clone/path naming; root implementation is under xdsk/xcart/xcdt. No disk images modified or completeness claim independently tested.

decisions.title: Final Fantasy Disch disassembly mirror
decisions.reason: Both this readme.txt and tracked Entroper/FF1Disassembly identify the same Disch v1.0 work with substantially identical author notes. No distinct reconstruction established.

decisions.title: Acorn DFS 2.45 superseded disassembly
decisions.reason: README explicitly calls repository redundant and directs to tracked acorn_1770_dfs_disassembly covering 2.24/2.25/2.26/2.29/2.45.

decisions.title: Caves of Oberon map research
decisions.reason: Detailed technical map write-up and images, but no reconstruction script or machine-readable map artifact found. Article repeats the same offset/range for distinct cell-block and block-grid sections and prints 8292 pixels for 1024 eight-pixel cells. Retain research lead pending reproducible extraction evidence, not a full game reconstruction.

notes: Parent-only pass across 44 platform/type search lanes. Broad and targeted searches combined where over-specific queries returned no candidates. Current catalogue and prior-decision screening plus title/author/successor review. Thirty-seven additions, two duplicate/superseded records and one reproducibility deferral. Inspected primary README, pinned source/tree and representative bodies. Includes extensionless assembly, .68k/.z80, .cp, .dis65 structured analysis, binary signature databases and HTML-embedded JavaScript: file extension alone is not an implementation classifier. Signature database decoded with base64 after non-UTF8 fetch failure; no candidate code executed. Generated naked assembly shims in .c files are classified as assembly, not C decompilation. SourceGen/JSON analysis that regenerates listings is distinct from a screenshot-only article. Retained explicit early-stage, unknown build/fidelity and original-asset dependencies.
